header.title: EM credit maturity turns returns to fundamentals, rewarding selective credit picking

s01_bottom_line.text: GSAM argues EM credit has matured into a more diverse, resilient asset class where the oil-price shock produced dispersion across credits rather than uniform stress, so returns are increasingly driven by fundamentals and credit selection rather than EM beta.
Investors should be selective in EM credit because credit selection now matters more than broad beta exposure.

The article offers no quantified spread, return or default data to verify the resilience and dispersion claims, so the thesis is a qualitative regime view an analyst would need to test against actual EM credit performance.

items.text: There are now more than 80 countries in the EM sovereign space.
The mix of energy exporters and importers within EM credit creates greater differentiation across issuers rather than broad-based selloffs.
In this shock cycle there has been dispersion across EM credits rather than uniform stress.
EM sovereign and corporate bonds weathered the oil-price shock with stability and solid performance.
Fundamental improvements may have reduced binary tail risk in EM credit, making credit selection matter more.
EM sovereigns now have deeper local-currency markets, stronger reserve buffers, more credible inflation policy and deeper domestic investor bases.
